# CORS credential theft on fp.coinbase.com due to arbitrary Origin reflection with credentials

**Template**: Web2
**Platform**: hackerone
**Scope**: https://fp.coinbase.com/
**Severity**: high | **CVSS**: 8.5 (`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`)
**CWE**: CWE-942 - Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains (CORS)
**Generated**: 2026-06-10T23:50:44Z

## Summary
The CORS policy on fp.coinbase.com reflects attacker-controlled Origin values and returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. The scan confirmed arbitrary origin reflection, trusted-suffix bypass variants, wildcard-subdomain variants, and null-origin handling on the same host. This allows a malicious website to issue credentialed browser requests to the affected API surface when a victim is logged in.

## Affected endpoint/feature
https://fp.coinbase.com/

## Auth context
Describe whether the endpoint requires authentication, which role was used, and whether the action is cross-user or unauthenticated.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Send a request to https://fp.coinbase.com/ with Origin: https://evil-attacker-sim.com.
2. Observe HTTP 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil-attacker-sim.com.
3. Observe Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
4. Repeat with related attacker-controlled origins such as https://notcoinbase.com and https://coinbase.com.evil.com.
5. The attached evidence bundle contains the scanner request/response evidence and the confirmed CORS_CREDENTIAL_THEFT chain.

Confirmed scanner evidence:
CORS probe to: https://fp.coinbase.com
Sent header: Origin: https://evil-attacker-sim.com
Response status: 200
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil-attacker-sim.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

## Expected result
The application should reject unauthorized or malformed access and preserve the intended security boundary.

## Actual result
GET https://fp.coinbase.com
  Origin: https://evil-attacker.com -> ACAO=https://evil-attacker.com ACAC=true
CONFIRMADO: Origin controlado pelo atacante refletido com credentials:true — credenciais cross-origin possíveis.

Attack chain confirmada: CORS_CREDENTIAL_THEFT
Severidade efetiva: high
Status da simulacao: confirmed
Evidencia da simulacao:
CORS probe to: https://fp.coinbase.com
Sent header: Origin: https://evil-attacker-sim.com
Response status: 200
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil-attacker-sim.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: (not set)

CONFIRMED: Server reflects attacker-controlled origin AND allows credentials. Cross-origin authenticated requests to this endpoint are possible.

## Impact
A malicious origin can read responses to credentialed cross-origin browser requests if the victim has valid Coinbase cookies for the affected host/API. This can expose authenticated user data or CSRF/token material returned by affected endpoints. The scanner did not exfiltrate user data; it confirmed the browser security boundary is disabled by reflected ACAO plus ACAC:true.

Raw finding evidence:

```text
GET https://fp.coinbase.com/ com Origin: https://evil.com (origem arbitraria evil.com)
-> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.com (refletido/aceito)
-> Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```

## Remediation
Use an explicit allowlist of trusted origins. Do not reflect arbitrary Origin values. Do not return Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for untrusted origins. Treat null origins as untrusted unless a specific, documented use case requires them.

## Impact

A malicious origin can read responses to credentialed cross-origin browser requests if the victim has valid Coinbase cookies for the affected host/API. This can expose authenticated user data or CSRF/token material returned by affected endpoints. The scanner did not exfiltrate user data; it confirmed the browser security boundary is disabled by reflected ACAO plus ACAC:true.
